text:
Heaven never
takes a day off.
why: The Image: heaven moves with inexhaustible vigor, and the realized person strengthens without ceasing. (Not a line lesson: 1-2-3 would be three line lessons in a row. The critic's 'Heaven never stops.' is 19 characters.)

text:
Frost underfoot:
ice is coming.
why: Line 1: small signs now tell you what is coming later.

text:
Hard start?
Get help first.
source: series/characters.json#3: A sprout stands buried to its tip; it pushes up through the ground in three strains, then lies down as the character.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
Teachers don't
chase students.
why: The Judgment: it is not I who seek the youth, the youth seeks me. (Not the suggested line 2: 3, 4 and 5 would be three line lessons in a row.)

text:
In the rain?
Eat, rest, wait.
source: series/characters.json#5: A figure stands; a cloud forms above and rain falls on it; it waits; the rain stops, the cloud comes down and the figure lies down under it.
why: The screen shows rain already falling, so the question now matches the picture. 'Eat, rest, wait' is the Image's 飲食宴樂, and the figure lying down at the end reads as rest. (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Won the belt,
lost it by noon.
why: Line 6: a win taken by fighting is stripped away before the morning is out.

text:
Unseen water
under the earth.
why: Accepted: water within the earth is the army, the people held in reserve.

text:
Choose who you
stand beside
source: series/characters.json#8: One figure stands; a second stands behind it, then walks up in three hops to stand close beside it; they lie down together as the character.
why: A second figure walking up to stand beside the first is 比 (holding together). (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Wheels come off,
the couple glares.
why: Line 3: the cart throws its spokes and husband and wife glare at each other; when something structural breaks, people on the same side turn on each other.

text:
Stood on a tiger's
tail. Not bitten.
why: The Judgment: treading on the tiger's tail, it does not bite the person. Both readers read the old text as a harmless tail; it has to say someone stands on the tail and the tiger still does not bite.

text:
No flat ground
without a slope.
why: Line 3: no level plain without slopes. Good times tilt, and that is normal.

text:
The good leave,
the petty move in.
why: Why things are stuck: the great departs, the small arrives, and the people who care are the ones pushed out.

text:
Parted, they weep.
Met, they laugh.
why: Line 5: fellowship first weeps and wails, then laughs when the armies manage to meet. Both readers got sad-then-happy but not that the tears come from being apart and the laughter from meeting.

text:
Big cart, loaded,
somewhere to go.
why: Having a lot is only useful when it has a load to carry and a place to take it.

text:
Level the heaps,
fill the holes.
why: The Image: the mountain within the earth reduces what is excessive and increases what is lacking.

text:
Shout about it
and it goes wrong.
why: Line 1: proclaiming your enthusiasm is adverse.

text:
Even thunder
rests in the lake.
why: LAKE over THUNDER: 'Thunder within the lake', energy resting in stillness. The picture itself backs the short's 'go in, rest', like 'Unseen water under the earth'.

text:
Found rot?
Clean it out.
source: series/characters.json#18: Worms breed in a shut bowl, swarm up and pour out.
why: The worm swarm in the bowl is the strongest drawing in the set. The sentence now teaches what the hexagram asks for, which is fixing the decay, not just a warning that it happens. (Scored 9 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Lean down. Care
for your people.
source: series/characters.json#19: A figure with a big eye stands, leans down, and three small squares light up under it one by one; then it lies down as the character.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json).

text:
Look like a guest,
not an inspector.
why: Approved: at line 4 the supported move is to be the sovereign's guest, observing with a visitor's courtesy.

text:
Warn clearly,
then bite.
why: FIRE over THUNDER: the kings made penalties clear and established the law, so clarity comes first and the bite second.

text:
A white horse?
It's a suitor.
why: Line 4: the white horse that looks like an attacker is a suitor. Something striking arriving is not always a threat.

text:
Falling apart?
Shore up the base.
source: series/characters.json#23: A knife stands beside a block; pieces fall off the block one by one until only its base stands; then both lie down as the character.
why: Pieces come off the block in frames 4 to 6, so 'falling apart' matches the screen, and 'shore up the base' is the Image's 上以厚下安宅, advice the viewer can use. The other options only describe the collapse. (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Midwinter: rest.
The light returns.
why: The Image: thunder within the earth is return, so the kings closed the passes at the solstice and no one travelled. Both readers asked why they stayed home: the stillness lets what is coming back return.

text:
Did nothing wrong,
still lost the ox.
why: Line 3: the tethered ox is taken by a traveller; innocence does not protect you from loss. The critic's own wording. Needs 26 or 27 off 'line'.

text:
Cap the calf's
horns early.
why: Line 4: a board on the young bull's horns, supremely good, is restraint put in place before there is harm.

text:
Stop staring at
someone's plate.
why: Line 1 sets down its own spirit tortoise to gape at someone else's meal: envy traded for self-sufficiency.

text:
In over your head.
Not your fault.
why: Line 6, over Hokusai's wave: wading too deep, the water covers the head. Adverse, but no fault.

text:
Don't get used
to the pit.
why: Line 1: entering the pit within the pit, adverse; the synthesis names people who settle into their crisis.

text:
At sunset, don't
party or wail.
why: Drumming and singing and lamenting old age are both adverse responses to the setting sun.

text:
It starts in
the big toes.
why: Line 1: 'Influence in the big toes.' The critic's repeated suggestion. Needs 30 or 32 off 'line'.

text:
Change shape,
keep your course
source: series/characters.json#32: Two lines rise; between them a moon goes from new to full and back, then sets into them; a heart is drawn beside it.
why: The moon changing shape between two steady lines shows constancy through change; the current line needs context. (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Leaving? Take your
people with you.
why: Line 3: a tangled retreat goes well if you keep your dependents with you instead of cutting them loose.

text:
Power in the toes:
don't kick yet.
why: Line 1: power in the toes, advancing is adverse though the wish is sincere. Concrete and a little funny. Needs 33 or 35 off 'line'.

text:
Sneak like a
squirrel? Seen.
why: Line 4: progressing like a squirrel, skulking and grabbing, is strained because everyone can see it for what it is. Both readers could not tell what the squirrel does wrong.

text:
Dark times?
Dim your light.
source: series/characters.json#36: A window rises; beside it a full moon shines, then wanes to a thin crescent that stays lit, and sets into the moon's strokes.
why: On screen the moon mostly dims, and a lit crescent is not clearly visible, so the sentence should say what is shown. 'Dim your light' does that and is the Image's 用晦而明, with no history needed. (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Whoever feeds them
holds the family.
why: Line 2: the one who stays in and feeds everyone is the center of the family, which Chardin's mother at the table shows at a glance.

text:
Not an attacker,
a suitor.
why: Line 6: what looked like a threat was someone coming to propose.

text:
Go on: blocked.
Come back: praise.
why: Line 1: 'Going forward: obstruction. Coming back: praise.' The critic's repeated suggestion. Needs 38 or 40 off 'line'.

text:
Untie it.
Forgive, then go.
source: series/characters.json#40: The ox and its horn are drawn; a knife rises beside them; the horn lifts free and hovers.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
Two small baskets
are enough.
why: The Judgment asks how to make the offering and answers with two small baskets.

text:
Let your gain
spill over
source: series/characters.json#42: A bowl rises; water fills it and spills over the far rim.
why: The character: water spilling over a full bowl, as the example short showed (special character-42). Chosen by the author over the line 5 lesson "Be kind. Don't keep score."

text:
Tell your own
town first.
why: Before a breakthrough, the Judgment says notify your own city.

text:
A lean pig kicks.
Tie it early.
why: Line 1: the small thing that looks harmless still struggles, so restrain it at the first sign.

text:
One handshake,
laughter again.
why: Line 1: after confusion, one handclasp restores laughter, so don't worry about the arguments.

text:
Go see someone
above you.
why: The Judgment says to use this time to see the great person, without worry.

text:
Boxed in?
Hold to your aim.
source: series/characters.json#47: A tree stands; walls rise round it; it is pressed flat inside them.
why: The clip ends with the tree boxed in, not growing, so 'keep growing' said the opposite of what the viewer just saw. 'Hold to your aim' matches the final frame and is the Image's 致命遂志. (Scored 8.5 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Towns move.
The well stays.
source: series/characters.json#48: Four beams rise as the well's frame; the water in the middle ripples on every beat.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
For a revolution,
a new calendar.
why: Fire in the lake is revolution, and the Image answers it by organizing the calendar and the seasons.

text:
Set the pot firm,
then cook.
source: series/characters.json#50: The legs rise; a fire is lit among them; the bowl, drawn high above, drops onto them.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7.5 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
First fear,
then laughter.
why: The Judgment puts terror and laughter in sequence: the shock comes, then the laugh.

text:
Stop. Stay
where you stand.
source: series/characters.json#52: A figure with a big eye stands, turns round to look back, holds still, turns forward again and lies down as the character.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
Goose in a tree?
Find flat footing.
why: A goose can't grip a branch; in the wrong place it looks for a flat perch, and there is no fault.

text:
The princess wore
the plainer dress.
why: The emperor's daughter dressed plainer than her attendant, and it resolves well.

text:
A huge house,
and no one home.
why: Line 6: so abundant his dwelling, peering through the gate, no one there for three years. The critic's suggestion. Needs 54 or 56 off 'line'.

text:
Far from home,
be a good guest
source: series/characters.json#56: People under a flag are drawn standing far off; they walk toward you in four hops, then lie down as the character.
why: The figure hopping toward you reads as travel. The sentence now carries the Judgment and Image, which say a wanderer succeeds by being modest and careful. 'Travel light' is not in the text. (Scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment.json.)

text:
Say it too often,
it grates.
why: Line 3, repeated penetration brings friction: repeating has a limit, past which the listener pushes back.

text:
Laugh and learn
with friends.
source: series/characters.json#58: A figure's mouth rises open; the two lines above it lift out of it and float, bobbing, like laughter.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 8 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json).

text:
Drop your faction,
more will gather.
why: Dissolving your own group supremely resolves well: dispersion creates accumulation, more than any faction could hold.

text:
A lake holds only
so much water.
why: Water over the lake: knowing your capacity is what keeps you from flooding.

text:
Truth even reaches
pigs and fish.
why: The Judgment opens with piglets and fish: real sincerity reaches even them.

text:
Missed the king?
See the minister.
why: Not reaching the ruler, meeting the minister: in a small time the tier below is the right channel, no fault.

text:
Done? Now guard
against trouble.
source: series/characters.json#63: A figure stands; a bowl rises beside it; the meal done, the figure turns its back on the bowl, holds, turns again and lies down as the character.
why: The character, with the best of the round 4 candidates (scored 7.5 in series/critic/lessons/treatment-candidates.json). Under 8: the critics fault the drawing, not the sentence.

text:
Almost across,
the fox gets wet.
why: The little fox has almost crossed and wets its tail: the last step is where it goes wrong.
